question: Does the exact stopped e5ed current Pages DATA item expose the known shortGUID field through the existing authenticated exact-ID Drive metadata read, and is its captured revision still current after the failed Apple open?
prediction: The read returns the scoped item metadata categories or a fixed refusal. shortGUID absence or presence alone does not establish the cause of Apple refusal or native editor readiness.

endpoint.calls: One exact-ID call. A second exact-ID read only if the first retains the recorded revision. No parent/app-container enumeration, download, manifest or model request.

time: Fresh Root-owned original 600 seconds with 45 seconds cleanup reserve; each exact metadata call capped by remaining original active time and 60 seconds. This does not reopen either prior write/UI window.
safe_output: Exact item, bounded revision and FILE type; receipt revision match; fixed categories for shortGUID and historically evidenced primitive fields; fixed docwsid/extension/zone matches. No field values, arbitrary field names, URLs, sharing tokens, cookies or raw bodies.
limits: No editor readiness or manifest/model initialization result.
No inference that shortGUID absence caused the failed Apple open.
No claim that metadata-only fields prove DATA or PACKAGE representation.
No cloud mutation, journal, writer, ACK, replay, Apple reopen or session persistence.
Actual HTTP request count is uninstrumented; only method-call count is reported.

output_scope.metadata_stable: Equality of sanitized metadata projections only. It does not prove raw metadata, shortGUID value or lastOpenTime unchanged.
output_scope.exact_metadata_stable: The same limited projection equality, not editor admission or full provider-body preservation.
output_scope.receipt_revision_changed: Stops after the first exact metadata call if captured ETag differs. No second call or old-revision byte claim.

assessment: Subsequent exact metadata reports a changed ETag and absent shortGUID. Neither absence nor revision change establishes the Apple refusal cause, DATA/PACKAGE representation or current raw bytes. One metadata method call; second refused by design on revision change.
